What Rangeelu Gujarat Is

A stage Gujarati culture deserves.

Rangeelu Gujarat started because we wanted to celebrate Gujarati culture properly. On a stage it deserved. With artists who care about what they perform, and a community that shows up because it matters to them.

This is not culture as costume or backdrop. It is the real thing — music, dance, craft, food and heritage rooted in what Gujarati tradition actually is. Handled with respect. Presented with pride.

British Gujaratis, the wider South Asian community, and anyone who wants to understand and celebrate this culture: you do not need to know the songs to join in. That is the whole point.

Cultural integrity, not costume
Gujarati culture is presented with rooted meaning. Not as trend, not as decoration.
No judgement, no gatekeeping
Any experience level, any background, anyone you bring with you. You are welcome.
Professional quality, community heart
The artistic bar is high. The atmosphere is warm. Both can be true.
Built to last, not just a highlight reel
Performances are captured. Stories are documented. The collection grows with each edition.

More Than a Festival

The stories don't
disappear
after one night.

Supported by
The heritage projects at Rangeelu Gujarat are made possible with support from The National Lottery Heritage Fund.

Rangeelu Gujarat is the umbrella under which Red Lotus Events carries forward some of its most important heritage work. What we capture, we keep. Songs, stories, voices — documented so they remain findable for the next generation.

This is what passing it forward looks like. Not just a festival poster. A growing collection on YouTube. A library people can return to years from now.

Heritage Project · Under Rangeelu Gujarat
Baa Ni Varta
Oral history recordings capturing the voices and memories of older generations. Growing as a permanent, searchable collection on YouTube.
Videos Coming Soon
Heritage Project · Under Rangeelu Gujarat
Lagna Geet
Traditional Gujarati wedding songs documented with translations, cultural meanings and recordings — so younger generations can find them, understand them, and feel they belong to a living tradition.
Videos Coming Soon
Heritage Project · Under Rangeelu Gujarat
Diu Daman Migration Story
Migration stories from the British Gujarati community becoming productions and recorded heritage — for community audiences and future access.

Community Voices

What it means
to be there.

"

Rangeelu Gujarat is the one event where I feel completely at home. The music, the Garba, the people — it feels like our community finally has a stage that reflects who we really are.

Kavita Mistry
Harrow, London
"

I travelled down from Manchester for it and I would do it again every time. Nothing up here comes close to the standard Rangeelu Gujarat sets. It is the real thing.

Alpesh Varsani
Manchester
"

My children experienced our Gujarati heritage in a way that school and the mandir alone cannot give them. They came home asking questions I had not heard from them before.

Meena Patel
Brent, London
"

The Garba night was traditional in the way it should be. Not Bollywood. The songs we grew up hearing. I felt it in my chest. That is what culture feels like when it is done with care.

Rajan Desai
Leicester
"

We come as a family every time — three generations of us. My mum loves the heritage performances, my kids love the energy, and I love that we are all in the same place feeling the same thing.

Sonal Shah
Barnet, London
"

Rangeelu Gujarat does not feel like it is trying to be something. It just is. Rooted, warm, and brilliantly put together. We are proud to support it every year.

Nikhil Bhatt
Harrow, London
